shots.say: How does a big rocket fly up, up into the sky?
No wings to flap! Whoosh, through the clouds!
Hi! I'm Gizmo. Let's find out how rockets fly!
Gizmo Explains!
Welcome to my lab, rocket fans!
Today we look inside a rocket, step by step.
Here is my model rocket. A pointy nose, and fins.
Inside, a rocket carries fuel. The engine uses the fuel.
What does the engine turn the fuel into? Hot gas, or ice cream?
Hot gas! The engine turns its fuel into hot gas.
Then it pushes the gas out of its back. Whoosh!
Out the back? Hmm. What happens next?
The gas goes down. Which way does the rocket go? Up, or down?
Up! The gas goes down, so the rocket goes up!
Let's watch a real rocket, on its launch pad.
The gas pushes the rocket the other way. Up it goes!
It is a push, and a push back. Push, and push back!
Press your hands together, like this. Do they push back?
Scientists say it simply. Every push has a push back!
Say it with me. Gas goes down! Rocket goes up!
Crouch down low, like a rocket. Ready? Blast off!
What comes out of a rocket's engine? Hot gas, or water?
Hot gas! Fuel, hot gas, and a big push. Up, up, up!
Way up high, a rocket flies into space.
But wait! In space, there is no air at all.
No air? Then how can a rocket work up there? Hmm.
Look, a jet plane! A jet needs air from outside to work.
Its engines take in air, as it flies along.
Can a rocket work in space, where there is no air? Yes, or no?
Yes! A rocket engine does not need air.
It carries everything it needs, right inside the rocket!
Like packing a backpack for a trip. All inside!
Which one needs air from outside? The jet, or the rocket?
The jet! A rocket brings what it needs along.
Air from outside? The jet needs it. The rocket does not!
So a rocket engine works in space, where there is no air.
Now let's watch one more launch, from far away.
Let's count down for a launch! Ready? Three, two, one...
Blast off! Up it goes, higher and higher!
Up through the clouds, and out into space!
Say it with me. A rocket does not need air!
Rockets carry satellites like this one up into space.
Can you point to the satellite? Point!
Big rockets have a trick. They are built in parts.
Let's count the parts. One, two, three!
A heavy rocket needs a big push, to get off the ground.
When the bottom part runs out of fuel, it drops away.
Bye-bye, bottom part! Now the next part starts its engine.
Is it easier to run with a heavy bag, or with no bag?
Is the rocket lighter now, or heavier?
Lighter! A lighter rocket can go much higher.
Up, and up, and up it goes!
Stack your fists, one on top of the other, like rocket parts!
This trick is called staging. It helps rockets reach space.
And even all the way to the Moon! Wow!
What does a big rocket drop as it flies? An empty part, or its nose?
An empty part! Drop it, and go higher.
Look how high we are! There is the Earth, way down below.
Say it together. Drop a part, go higher!
And some rockets take astronauts into space!
Wave to the rocket! Bye-bye, rocket! Have a good trip!
Quiz time! Let's remember what we learned.
What comes out of a rocket's engine? Hot gas, or bubbles?
Hot gas! The gas goes down, and the rocket goes up.
Does a rocket engine need air? Yes, or no?
No! It carries everything it needs.
When the bottom part drops away, is the rocket lighter, or heavier?
Lighter! So it can go much higher.
Gas goes down, rocket goes up! Thanks for exploring with me!
Gizmo Explains!
